acceptance: A unit test feeds a 503 ServerBusy then success to the pr-arm verdict download and shows pr-arm evaluates the verdict; a persistent 503 still refuses after the bounded budget.
Each listed single-attempt caller either retries transient failures with bounded backoff or records why it must not; nightly-v2.yml:494 no longer hides a failed download.
If the verdict moves to a check-run output or status, pr-arm reads it there and the artifact path is removed, not kept as a fallback.
Coordinates with pr-arm-cut-repeated-github-reads-20261117 and pr-arm-github-rate-limit-backoff-20261112 on the shared read helper; no read is cached across wait cycles.
context: Found 2026-11-17 by a read-only root-cause investigation of the egress 503. Guardrails: linked worktree (make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight), never the primary clone; one PR per repo; no live-cloud runs or credentials in Git or logs; heavy work only via lock-taking entry points or make heavy-run after make heavy-status; never start deliberate host load; comment policy; changelog.d fragment for user-facing change. Re-verify every cited file and line before acting; they are hints.
description:
Problem: on 2026-11-17 `make pr-arm` for PR #4274 refused with `HTTP 503: Egress is over the account limit` while downloading the 535-byte artifact fast-duration-verdict-4274-c6d657102. The 503 is Azure ServerBusy on GitHub's shared multi-tenant results storage (productionresultssa9), not a BenchBox quota; githubstatus showed no incident and a retry about 25 minutes later succeeded. scripts/pr_arm.py:277 runs the download once and lines 279-280 turn any non-zero exit into a refusal. Azure's documented guidance is bounded exponential backoff on 503. The same single-attempt pattern is in scripts/release_artifact_consumer.py:854, scripts/release_reuse_uat_evidence.py:386, scripts/sqlglot_delivery.py:341, scripts/trunk_duration_trend.py:365, scripts/trunk_uat.py:564 and .github/workflows/fast-duration-baseline-refresh.yml:101,247,251; .github/workflows/nightly-v2.yml:494 also hides the failure with `|| true`. Same day, a pr-arm for PR #4276 refused on `dial tcp ...: i/o timeout` reading the develop ruleset; a retry armed at once.

Outcome: transient 5xx, ServerBusy and network timeouts on these reads are retried within a bounded budget, never treated as a pass; a persistent failure still refuses with a clear outcome line. Prefer publishing the fast-duration verdict as a check-run output or commit status so arming does not depend on blob storage at all.
